item.title: Non residential wastewater
item.description:
One of the biggest opportunities for reducing the environmental footprint of primary industry exists in the handling and reduction of wastewater.

The headline example of this at the moment is probably AI data centres; the media are describing an AI landscape where every model interaction supposedly requires a vast amount of water and electricity to cool these vast computer hubs. Water is not actually consumed in this process (strictly speaking, there a few processes that actually consume water, e.g., photosynthesis); however, it is considered waste because it is a vector transporter of heat, where heat is the waste product.

item.title: Constituents
item.description:
Did you know there’s a spotify playlist called “Songs About Water”?

Well, when I sat down to write this blog, I thought it might put me in the mood to write about water. And then I thought Wait, is this a common experience? This playlist has over 1k saves on Spotify, are all these people writing about water? Why are there so many songs about water? Why doesn’t the playlist contain Every Teardrop Is a Waterfall by Coldplay? Do these artists also sing about air?

item.title: What else am I doing?
item.description:
I am currently working on my environmental engineering honours project at UWA, investigating the relationship between purchasing power and thermal comfort in the housing market and aims to answer the question: If I cannot afford the median house price, will I be forced to buy a house with a hotter associated microclimate?

While findings might be confronting (especially to someone who would like to buy into the market like myself), I am excited about what this project can uncover. If we know the impacts of our house on our health, we can make informed decisions about where we choose to buy and what (if any) renovations we can do to improve conditions.
